summary: Full backend + frontend test of JARVIS app. 13/13 pytest cases passed (health, status, chat, sessions CRUD, validation, and all 5 routing-classification cases). Playwright UI flow passed end-to-end: page load, 5 status cards, prompt suggestion populating input, sending a chat and getting a categorized JARVIS reply, session badge update, sidebar listing, New chat reset, loading prior session messages, and deleting a session.
critical_code_review_comments: DELETE /api/sessions/{id} always returns 200 even if the session does not exist - consider 404 for missing IDs (minor, not blocking).

_strip_code_fence does not strip the language tag (e.g. 'json') if the LLM returns ```json fenced output; current json.loads will fail and silently fall back to category='general'. In practice gpt-4o-mini did not fence in our run, but a stricter strip (e.g. drop first line entirely after ```) would be safer.
is_new check fires an extra Mongo find_one on every chat call even when session_id is None - tiny optimization: skip the lookup when req.session_id is None.
seed_data_creation: Tests create temporary sessions via /api/chat and clean them up via DELETE /api/sessions/{id}.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_jarvis_api.py reads REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env and exercises every route. Routing accuracy parametrize runs 5 LLM calls; each chat in tests costs a real Emergent LLM credit, so re-run sparingly. Frontend uses data-testid attributes throughout (status-card-{name}, chat-input, send-btn, new-chat-btn, session-item-{id}, delete-session-{id}, category-badge-{cat}, message-{role}-{id}, prompt-suggestion-{slug}).
